plan: [ With independent private values and a second‑price (Vickrey) auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if you accidentally win; underbidding risks losing when winning would have been profitable. There’s only 1 round and no history to exploit. Therefore, set the maximum price at exactly my value so I win iff the second-highest bid is below my value, capturing surplus equal to value minus that second-highest bid. ]

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ bids. There is no prior-round history to exploit in round 1 of 1. With value $29 drawn uniformly from $0–$49, I should bid 29 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 29, paying that amount, ensuring non-negative profit.

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. It guarantees winning exactly when the second-highest bid is below your value and paying that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Overbidding risks paying above your value if others bid high; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value = 45 (uniform draws 0–49), the best long-run and round-specific strategy is to bid 45. No history to exploit in a single round; focus on truth-telling to maximize expected surplus. ]
